## VEED Clean Audio: Video Speech Cleanup — Workflow Guide

## Input Asset

- [veed_clean_audio_input_h3_omniref_person_dialogue_plus_noise.mp4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/veed_clean_audio_input_h3_omniref_person_dialogue_plus_noise.mp4)

## What This Workflow Does
Load Video → VEED Clean Audio (in Video) → Save Video.

Swap the soundtrack of a clip for a cleaned copy of its own speech: the node removes background noise, music and sound effects, washes the pauses clean, then optionally lifts the level to a target loudness. The picture is left alone — only the audio track comes back different, as 48 kHz mono speech.

Best for: talking-head footage, interviews, phone and field recordings, B-roll with scratch dialogue, and any clip that has to be intelligible before it is cut, dubbed or localized.

## How to Use
1. Load the clip in Load Video. It has to carry an audio track; a silent clip stops with an error instead of inventing sound.
2. Set strength on the node: how much noise is removed under the voice. The default 0.874 is the tuned value.
3. Pick loudness. normalize (default) evens the level out to the target_lufs you set; keep input level leaves the gain as recorded.
4. Run the workflow. VEED sends the same picture back with the cleaned track, and Save Video writes it as video/VEED_Clean_Audio_Video with an auto container and codec.

## Limits
- Video up to 1799 seconds (just under 30 minutes) per run.
- Delivered audio is 48 kHz mono, so a stereo or surround source is folded down and the saved file carries mono sound.
- The clip must have an audio track; without one the node raises "The video has no audio track to clean."
- The picture is not a knob: the node has no resolution or frame-rate setting, it returns the video the service sends back, and Save Video keeps the compatible source stream under auto.
- Speech only: music and effects are removed together with the noise, not preserved.
- strength runs 0.0 to 1.0, default 0.874. Lower keeps more room tone behind the voice; pauses between words are always fully cleaned, and values above the default change little.
- target_lufs runs -40 to -8 LUFS, default -19. Peaks are capped at -1.1 dBTP, so loud targets stop early: typical speech settles around -15 LUFS instead of reaching the number you typed.
- Keep input level skips the gain stage entirely, so only denoising happens.

## Tips
1. Give it the cleanest take you have: denoising cannot restore words that were never recorded, and heavy clipping stays clipped.
2. If the voice sounds hollow or gated, lower strength a step; if room noise still leaks through under the words, raise it. Only the speech-level noise follows this knob, so a noisy tail between sentences is handled regardless.
3. Normalize once, at the end of the chain. Running several loudness passes in a row just re-limits an already limited file.
4. Keep the source clip around: the template has one video output, so the clean take replaces the original in the graph instead of sitting next to it.
5. Judge the result with picture: pauses should fall to near silence while the voice keeps its breath and the lips still line up, since only the soundtrack changed.
